Oration

/aw-RAY-shun/ - rhymes with vacation · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Oration means a formal, ceremonious public speech.

The union's founding charter is read aloud each May in a full oration, delivered from memory by whichever steward wins the honor.

Worked Example

The debate team's coach screens a filmed oration from the 1963 nationals: fourteen minutes without notes, each argument rising out of the last, the pauses placed like stair landings, and a final sentence that lands like a gavel.

An oration is not just any speech; it is a formal, ceremonious one — built, rehearsed, and delivered for an occasion. Remarks can be scribbled on a napkin and a toast can be winged, but an oration has architecture, and the audience is meant to feel the design.

How Oration Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

formal address

formal address: a prepared speech for an occasion, said plainly

declamation

declamation: a speech delivered with studied, formal force

Antonyms

offhand remarks

offhand remarks: unprepared comments tossed out in the moment

small talk

small talk: light conversation that carries no occasion's weight

How Strong Is It? — remarks → speech → oration

remarks vs. oration

remarks vs. oration: Remarks sit at the mild end — a few unpolished sentences that nobody expects to be built.

speech vs. oration

speech vs. oration: A speech stops short of an oration: it is prepared and public, but without the ceremonial build and rehearsed rhythms an oration demands.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — orat-

Root — orat-: to speak formally, plead (Latin orare)

Suffix — -ion

Suffix — -ion: noun: the act of

Put it together

Put it together: Orat- (to speak formally) + -ion = the act of formal speaking. Latin orare covered pleading in court and praying to the gods — speech aimed high on purpose. An oration keeps that aim: language dressed for the occasion.

Use the root in a new word: oracle

Use the root in a new word: oracle: Kings crossed the sea to ask the oracle a single question.

Word Choice

formal / historical

Oration is reserved for the fully ceremonious occasion — dedications, funerals of state, championship finals of rhetoric. Everyday prepared talks are speeches; a few unprepared words are remarks. Call something an oration and you promise architecture.
